public_health_question.v: What was the source of a gastrointestinal illness outbreak among patrons of a community swimming pool, and what was the role of C. difficile findings?

ev.q: PADOH issued pool closure orders and initiated an outbreak response to identify a source and prevent additional illnesses.
Escherichia coli O157:H7 Outbreak in Children with Clostridioides difficile Colonization Associated with an Improperly Treated Swimming Pool
this outbreak was likely the result of STEC infections among children, some of whom were colonized with C. difficile .

notes: Descriptive outbreak case series with no attack rates or exposed/unexposed comparison (pool visitor count unknown). Prevalence figures for asymptomatic C. difficile colonization are cited from other studies, not computed here. Pool inspection findings are compliance observations, not comparisons.
view_issues: Text says four received antibiotics for C. difficile, but the table shows Patient B received azithromycin, so only three received C. difficile–directed agents. Text says two patrons had STEC and C. difficile; the table caption says three presumed colonized.
